chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Abi Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him, while I was listening, saying: 'I pray the dawn prayer, then I remember God with all that I wish to remember of what is obligatory upon me. Then I wish to lay my side [to sleep] and sleep before the sunrise, but I dislike doing that.' He said, 'Why?' He said: 'I dislike that the sun rises from a place other than its place of rising.' He said, 'It is not obscure [in this regard]; look from where the dawn rises, and from there the sun rises. And there is no difficulty upon you to sleep if you have remembered God, the Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sleep after the Fajr prayer before sunrise?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Imam’s practical approach to removing unnecessary anxiety (haraj) in daily worship, specifically addressing the pre-Islamic Arab superstition that the sun might rise from the west as a sign of the Hour. By linking the sun’s rising point directly to the dawn’s emergence, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a clear astronomical and theological reassurance that allows the believer to rest without fear of missing the prayer time or incurring religious penalty.
